title: Lattice and Text to Lattice documentation register

authority.claimBoundary: This register describes the Lattice method at an architectural level and the bounded Text to Lattice implementation evidenced in this repository. It does not redistribute the exclusive register profile, certify universal conformance, or convert source tests into deployed proof.
authority.changePolicy: Stable identifiers persist. A claim changes here with cited evidence; a rendered filter, expansion, or downloaded view never changes authoritative state.
authority.marginalValuePolicy: Treat consequence multiplied by plausibility multiplied by lifecycle value as the decision boundary. Unusual findings remain eligible; low-consequence, implausible, lifecycle-poor work does not become release-blocking by novelty alone.
authority.exportPolicy: Markdown and HTML are deterministic projections of this register. Filtered browser exports are nonauthoritative reading views.

historicalBoundary.supersededArchitecture: Browser-local WebLLM inference with Turnstile admission and a renewable usage lease.
historicalBoundary.currentArchitecture: After explicit visitor authorization, one named same-origin /api/lattice capability performs a bodyless visitor-session setup and then exactly one content-bearing POST under the same browser Web Lock, followed by fixed server-side Hugging Face router calls served by Nscale for Qwen generation and DeepInfra for Llama verification.
historicalBoundary.evidencePolicy: Historical source identifiers, blueprint records, gate records, and qualification evidence remain available for audit, but they do not satisfy the current remote-service release gates.

conceptMap.description: A typed map of the upstream Lattice engine: who supplies authority, how meaning becomes a bounded output plan, how candidates clear protected gates, and where hosts and ecosystem applications remain responsible.

groups.label: Authority
groups.description: The caller and domain sources that establish meaning before expression.

groups.label: Semantic contract
groups.description: Typed atoms and relations that make preservation testable.

groups.label: Context and plan
groups.description: Explicit context, content layers, representations, priorities, and requested outputs.

groups.label: Realization
groups.description: Mapped proposals and the controlled literal baseline.

groups.label: Evaluation
groups.description: Engine gates, profile decisions, and deterministic selection.

groups.label: Output and evidence
groups.description: Plain-text results, receipts, and structural verification.

groups.label: Host boundary
groups.description: Presentation, source quality, privacy, and human review that stay outside the engine.

groups.label: Ecosystem
groups.description: Products that apply or interpret Lattice under their own contracts.

nodes.label: Lattice engine
nodes.caption: Meaning contract ≠ register ≠ realization ≠ presentation
nodes.definition: A local-first deterministic TypeScript engine that realizes and validates context-sensitive plain text from typed meaning, explicit context, declarative profiles, and traceable candidates.

nodes.label: Caller and domain authority
nodes.caption: Truth enters before expression
nodes.definition: The caller supplies structured claims, terminology, context, candidate provenance, and domain attestations. Lattice does not infer source truth, authority, or missing high-priority context.

nodes.label: Meaning contract
nodes.caption: Semantic authority in typed form
nodes.definition: A bounded contract gives each semantic obligation a stable identity, frame, criticality, delivery policy, protected fields, permitted evidence, and prohibited dependencies.

nodes.label: Semantic atoms
nodes.caption: Independently addressable obligations
nodes.definition: Actions, states, timings, conditions, consequences, prohibitions, uncertainties, recovery steps, and relations carry structured subjects, predicates, objects, polarity, modality, value, unit, and condition references.

nodes.label: Typed relations
nodes.caption: Before · after · requires · causes · contradicts
nodes.definition: Relations connect existing atoms and make protected order, dependency, causality, and contradiction explicit; unresolved references, invalid self-links, and incoherent cycles fail closed.

nodes.label: Register context
nodes.caption: Explicit, never ambient
nodes.definition: Domain, surface, mode, stakes, safety class, locale, audience, focalizer, channel capabilities, and execution limits arrive as validated input rather than time, locale, identity, network, or prior-run inference.

nodes.label: Content layer
nodes.caption: Operative · experiential · interpretive
nodes.definition: A requested layer determines which atoms must be explicit or may be inferable, while experiential and interpretive emphasis cannot contradict or conceal operative meaning.

nodes.label: Representation
nodes.caption: Standard · accessibility-equivalent
nodes.definition: Accessibility is another realization of the same relevant atoms, not a fourth narrative layer. Essential meaning cannot depend on unavailable imagery, color, sound, spatial inference, timing perception, or implication.

nodes.label: Protected priority
nodes.caption: Safety before ornament
nodes.definition: Safety, semantic fidelity, accessibility equivalence, required operative clarity, and authoritative domain correctness are hard gates that profile style and ranking cannot outweigh.

nodes.label: Profile and RSR boundary
nodes.caption: Declarative policy · protected license
nodes.definition: Profiles declare bounded predicates, validators, dependencies, conflicts, and lower-priority policy without executable transforms. The bundled Relational Systems Register remains separately licensed and is not reproduced here.

nodes.label: Output plan
nodes.caption: Requested layer × representation
nodes.definition: Normalized outputs are unique, ordered layer-and-representation pairs; accessibility equivalents pull in their standard pair, and safety-critical contexts require both operative representations.

nodes.label: Mapped candidate
nodes.caption: Untrusted proposal with atom evidence
nodes.definition: A host may propose bounded plain text, atom identifiers, and validation metadata. Candidate order and source do not authorize selection; unknown mappings and invented claims remain rejectable.

nodes.label: Literal baseline
nodes.caption: Controlled fallback, labeled literal
nodes.definition: When no mapped candidate targets an output, the engine constructs a deterministic realization from controlled literal forms or structured frames and never labels it full conformance.

nodes.label: Hard gates
nodes.caption: Failure cannot be averaged away
nodes.definition: Engine-owned checks reject uncovered atoms, protected drift, changed polarity or modality, quantity or unit change, unsafe dependencies, layer contradiction, accessibility gaps, and other registered structural failures.

nodes.label: Profile evaluation
nodes.caption: Applicability ≠ result
nodes.definition: Each rule records applied, suppressed, or inapplicable separately from pass, warn, fail, unknown, or not-applicable, so nonexecution cannot masquerade as satisfaction.

nodes.label: Lexicographic selection
nodes.caption: Priority tuple, then stable digest
nodes.definition: Admissible candidates are ranked lexicographically by protected priority, conformance, registered findings, and stable tie-break evidence; a stylistic gain cannot compensate for a hard failure.

nodes.label: Layered plain-text output
nodes.caption: Selected realization with bounded conformance
nodes.definition: Each output exposes its layer, representation, text, atom mapping, candidate source, conformance, coverage, findings, and rule decisions; the host still owns presentation.

nodes.label: Derivation receipt
nodes.caption: Reproducibility, not authenticity
nodes.definition: A canonical receipt binds input, engine and profile versions, outputs, candidates, decisions, assurance scope, and derivation digest without claiming that facts or history are authentic.

nodes.label: Structural verification
nodes.caption: Self-consistent, unauthenticated
nodes.definition: Receipt and result verification reject unsupported schemas, broken references, altered aggregates, and digest tampering while reporting that integrity is self-consistent and not externally authenticated.

nodes.label: Host application
nodes.caption: Candidate, UI, privacy, and persistence owner
nodes.definition: The host owns domain-source quality, mapped candidate production, sanitization, rendering, storage consent, privacy, interface accessibility, and any claims beyond the engine's declared trust scope.

nodes.label: Human and assistive-technology review
nodes.caption: Empirical judgment remains necessary
nodes.definition: Disabled users, assistive technologies, domain reviewers, and editors test accessibility, comprehension, truth, moral adequacy, and literary quality that deterministic structure cannot prove.

nodes.label: Text to Lattice
nodes.caption: Probabilistic remote wrapper, distinct authority model
nodes.definition: The hah.dev demonstrator sends visitor-authorized text through a same-origin API to fixed server-side Nscale-served Qwen generation and Nscale-served Llama verification models. It does not inherit the upstream engine's typed caller-authority guarantee and must state its weaker semantic and external-processing boundary separately.

nodes.label: FOG OF SEA
nodes.caption: Naval learning and operational uncertainty
nodes.definition: A host context that applies Lattice to naval learning, operational uncertainty, and accessible tactical interaction under its own domain and evidence responsibilities.

nodes.label: CHORUS
nodes.caption: Social and epistemic systems
nodes.definition: A host context that applies Lattice to social and epistemic systems while retaining its own simulation, claim, accessibility, and evidence boundaries.

nodes.label: Evenward
nodes.caption: Selected embodied guidance and care
nodes.definition: A host context that selectively applies Lattice to embodied guidance and care while remaining responsible for safety, privacy, presentation, and human validation.

skillMap.methodNote: This map adapts NN/g's competency-mapping form to an evidence inventory for the upstream Lattice engine at revision d6cc85b. It never rates a person, team member, or human proficiency. A score records the strongest evidence class for a system capability, not importance or artistic quality.

scale.label: Not claimed
scale.definition: The capability is outside the authorized product boundary or lacks a supported claim.

scale.label: Defined
scale.definition: A bounded requirement and intended evidence path exist.

scale.label: Implemented
scale.definition: Repository implementation exists; verification or lifecycle evidence remains incomplete.

scale.label: Internally verified
scale.definition: Maintainer-authored repository tests verify ordinary and boundary behavior.

scale.label: Adversarially verified
scale.definition: Self-authored adversarial repository evidence challenges realistic failure and tampering modes.

scale.label: Externally validated
scale.definition: Independent, production, longitudinal, or representative user evidence supports the claim across contexts.

capabilities.label: Semantic and relational modeling
capabilities.definition: Models independently identified atoms, protected frame fields, delivery obligations, terminology, prohibited claims, and before, after, requires, causes, and contradicts relations.
capabilities.evidence: The semantic core rejects unresolved conditions, invalid relation targets, contradictions, ordering cycles, and weakened protected meaning; adversarial fixtures challenge polarity, modality, quantity, units, uncertainty, order, and recovery.
capabilities.openBoundary: Typed contracts make declared meaning testable but do not prove source facts or interpret arbitrary prose.

capabilities.label: Context and audience modeling
capabilities.definition: Requires explicit domain, surface, mode, stakes, safety class, locale, audience, focalizer, channel, scene, and bounded execution context.
capabilities.evidence: Context validation rejects missing or unsupported high-priority values, bounds tags and limits, and never consults ambient identity, time, locale, network, or previous runs.
capabilities.openBoundary: Correctness still depends on the caller supplying adequate and truthful context; English-oriented resources limit locale scope.

capabilities.label: Layered content architecture
capabilities.definition: Keeps operative, experiential, and interpretive content obligations separate while allowing multiple representations of the same atoms.
capabilities.evidence: Output normalization, required-atom planning, cross-output checks, and adversarial layer-contradiction cases enforce the distinction.
capabilities.openBoundary: The engine evaluates supplied structured candidates; it does not generate novel literary prose or infer a layer from free-form text.

capabilities.label: Register and constraint architecture
capabilities.definition: Compiles versioned declarative profiles with bounded predicates, known validators, dependencies, conflicts, priorities, enforcement, and protected engine namespaces.
capabilities.evidence: Compilation rejects unknown fields, executable or unknown validators, cycles, undeclared conflicts, same-tier hard conflicts, protected priorities, and unresolved dependencies.
capabilities.openBoundary: A structurally valid profile is not proof of artistic quality; the bundled RSR remains separately licensed and is not inventoried here.

capabilities.label: Deterministic and bounded engineering
capabilities.definition: Normalizes bounded plain data, freezes compiled structures, ranks lexicographically, and excludes time, filesystem order, platform locale, network state, and ambient randomness from realization.
capabilities.evidence: Canonical digests, stable ordering, explicit execution limits, candidate-order invariance, and repeated adversarial requests demonstrate byte-identical derivation within the reviewed revision.
capabilities.openBoundary: Determinism holds for canonical requests and pinned engine/profile versions; hosts and external candidate producers need their own controls.

capabilities.label: Core security and trust boundary
capabilities.definition: Accepts bounded nonexecutable data, prevents profiles from rewriting semantic slots or running arbitrary code, rejects prohibited structures, and performs no runtime network, telemetry, or hidden persistence.
capabilities.evidence: Plain-data validation, restricted predicate syntax, known validator registration, protected priorities, fail-closed errors, and adversarial malformed-input cases exercise the core boundary.
capabilities.openBoundary: Hosts still own parsing duplicate-key rejection, output escaping, candidate trust, storage permission, network behavior, and UI security.

capabilities.label: Accessibility equivalence
capabilities.definition: Models accessibility-equivalent output as a representation of the same relevant atoms and suppresses imagery, color, sound, spatial, timing-perception, or implication dependencies where unavailable.
capabilities.evidence: Context protection, output normalization, atom delivery, hard gates, and cross-output parity are implemented and covered by maintainer-authored tests.
capabilities.openBoundary: Structural channel independence does not replace testing with disabled users, assistive technologies, or the host interface.

capabilities.label: Evidence and provenance
capabilities.definition: Records canonical inputs, versioned dependencies, candidate decisions, atom coverage, rule dispositions, findings, output digests, trust scope, and a reproducible derivation digest.
capabilities.evidence: Receipt and result verifiers enforce exact schemas, referential consistency, aggregate conformance, output binding, and tamper detection in adversarial fixtures.
capabilities.openBoundary: The receipt is self-consistent and unauthenticated; hashes do not establish truth, authorship, or historical authenticity.

capabilities.label: Adversarial verification
capabilities.definition: Challenges realistic contract, profile, candidate, ordering, accessibility, tampering, execution-bound, locale, and trust-scope failures rather than counting happy paths alone.
capabilities.evidence: The reviewed adversarial suite exercises candidate exhaustion, protected meaning, conflicts, malformed records, candidate-order independence, receipt tampering, and bounded failure behavior.
capabilities.openBoundary: The suite is self-authored repository evidence, not independent security review, formal proof, or production observation.

capabilities.label: Lifecycle and host integration
capabilities.definition: Uses stable versions, schemas, identifiers, profile digests, typed failures, verification functions, CLI boundaries, and explicit host duties to make integration and supersession inspectable.
capabilities.evidence: Architecture and requirements define extension, failure, verification, and host contracts; the reviewed engine exposes structured results and verification rather than presentation-side assertions.
capabilities.openBoundary: No score five is assigned: independent integration, production, longitudinal maintenance, and representative user evidence remain external.

serviceBlueprint.scenario: A visitor converts authorized prose into one bounded Lattice outcome through the disclosed remote capability.
serviceBlueprint.actor: A visitor using a secure, JavaScript-capable browser who is authorized to send the submitted text to the disclosed external service.
serviceBlueprint.goal: Receive a bounded checked result, a review-marked material draft, an unable-to-attempt outcome with no transformed text, or a finite machine-readable error after one deliberate external-processing submission.
serviceBlueprint.methodNote: The blueprint follows NN/g's service-blueprint separation of user action, visible service, backstage process, and support process, then makes the client/server, provider, evidence, retention, and recovery boundaries explicit.

lines.label: Line of interaction
lines.meaning: What the visitor directly authorizes, acts upon, cancels, and receives.

lines.label: Line of visibility
lines.meaning: The interface discloses external processing and bounded outcomes; prompts, provider calls, validation, and repair remain implementation details.

lines.label: Line of trust and network
lines.between: Browser, same-origin API, and external provider
lines.meaning: After explicit confirmation, the browser sends exactly text, requested_mode, and schema_version 1 to same-origin /api/lattice; the Worker alone holds HF_TOKEN and calls the fixed Hugging Face router and Nscale-served generator and Nscale-served verifier.

lines.label: Line of accountability
lines.meaning: Source and tests support repository claims; current remote deployment, live-provider behavior, provider retention, and manual exercises require separate evidence.

lifecycleOwners.responsibility: Govern the method, licensed profile boundary, version, and authorized conformance claims.
lifecycleOwners.handoffEvidence: A cited upstream revision, applicable license terms, and an explicit public claim boundary.

lifecycleOwners.responsibility: Keep input bounds, explicit external-processing consent, the origin-wide Web Lock across content-free visitor-session setup and exactly one content request, exact request construction, accessibility, cancellation, and public outcome behavior aligned with the requirements.
lifecycleOwners.handoffEvidence: Exact source revision, named capability and shared-lock tests, modal lifecycle tests, and built static artifact inspection.

lifecycleOwners.responsibility: Validate method, path, origin, the two closed media envelopes, schema, modes, content limits, and the only permitted browser-owned quota cookie; establish or preserve that cookie without admission or provider work; reject missing-cookie content before both; keep HF_TOKEN and VISITOR_COOKIE_SECRET server-only; atomically enforce 30 accepted transformations globally per UTC day and 3 per cooperating canonical client with an ordinary persistent browser cookie jar per UTC day without IP, fingerprint, or content identity; state intentional cookie clearing and uncooperative callers outside the per-browser claim while keeping the global bound exact; count admitted failures without refund or an in-pipeline shared quota recheck; and return bounded no-store responses.
lifecycleOwners.handoffEvidence: Reviewed Worker revision, exact route, secret, Durable Object, rate-shaper, and cookie inventory; setup/no-admission and missing-cookie pre-admission tests; instrumented admission tests; bounded live probes; value-free Set-Cookie metadata; and deployed response captures proving 32 provider calls at most per admitted request and 960 at most from admitted requests per UTC day.

lifecycleOwners.surface: Hugging Face and Nscale provider boundary
lifecycleOwners.responsibility: Keep egress fixed to the Hugging Face chat-completions router, Qwen generation, and Llama verification; require closed structured output and deterministic fail-closed host validation; prohibit user-selected targets and provider or model fallback.
lifecycleOwners.handoffEvidence: Exact endpoint and model identities; server-only secret proof; adapter allowlist, bounded structured-output, and host-validation tests; provider terms review; and bounded live-provider evidence.

lifecycleOwners.responsibility: Define no application storage, raw-content logging, cache, queue, or analytics sink for source, prompts, candidates, results, or raw provider bodies; keep content only in bounded request memory.
lifecycleOwners.handoffEvidence: Static sink scan, binding inventory, no-store response capture, log configuration review, and an explicit provider-policy limitation.

lifecycleOwners.surface: Static Pages, response policy, and documentation export
lifecycleOwners.responsibility: Publish concise external-processing semantics, deterministic projections, working links, escaped register content, matching integrity metadata, and a browser policy that permits only the named same-origin capability.
lifecycleOwners.handoffEvidence: Documentation drift check, SHA-256 manifest, generated-page inspection, route tests, and live CSP and Permissions-Policy captures.

lifecycleOwners.responsibility: Accept or reject residuals and approve only the exact source, configuration, artifacts, provider controls, and current remote deployment evidence reviewed.
lifecycleOwners.handoffEvidence: A dated gate record naming the revision and artifact digests, with GATE-02 and GATE-06 satisfied by current remote evidence rather than historical browser-local evidence.

lifecycleOwners.responsibility: Use text they are authorized to process, avoid restricted information, deliberately choose Process with external service, and decide whether disclosed external-provider residuals are acceptable.
lifecycleOwners.handoffEvidence: Visible purpose, transmission, restricted-information, provider, retention-boundary, outcome, and residual disclosures before submission.

stages.visitorAction: Opens Text to Lattice and reads the purpose, limits, external-processing warning, restricted-information warning, and canonical documentation link.
stages.frontstage: The dialog names the same-origin API, external service, fixed model roles, application no-retention rule, provider limitation, and finite outcomes before accepting a submission.
stages.backstage: The interface resolves the named lattice.remote capability and local input prerequisites without contacting /api/lattice.
stages.supportNetwork: No transformation request or provider call occurs on open, edit, validation failure, dismissal, or cancellation before submission.
stages.evidenceRecovery: Unsupported capability yields a precise unavailable state while the semantic documentation remains available.
stages.dataCrossing: No submitted prose crosses a network boundary.
stages.failure: The browser cannot satisfy the secure-context, JavaScript, segmentation, or named-capability requirement.
stages.recovery: Read the method and limitation record or use a compatible browser; no text was transmitted.

stages.visitorAction: Enters one to 700 Unicode-aware words and chooses a supported requested mode.
stages.frontstage: The shared counter and concise inline validation expose only actionable limits.
stages.backstage: The browser validates Unicode structure, 12,000 code units, 65,536 request bytes, passage and work-group ceilings, the requested mode, and schema version before enabling submission.
stages.supportNetwork: The same-origin API and provider remain untouched during editing and failed preflight.
stages.evidenceRecovery: The source stays editable; rejection is local, bounded, and does not truncate or relabel text.
stages.dataCrossing: Source and structural findings remain in the browser document.
stages.failure: Input exceeds a published boundary or contains unsafe structure.
stages.recovery: Revise the source locally; no remote work began.

stages.visitorAction: Reviews the warning and deliberately chooses Process with external service, or chooses Cancel.
stages.frontstage: The action states that the text leaves hah.dev and that Hugging Face, Nscale, and their infrastructure process it under their own policies.
stages.backstage: Only the explicit submission action acquires the origin-wide browser Web Lock and creates the content-free setup plus exact content request; there is no implicit submit, prefetch, or background send, and no automatic retry.
stages.supportNetwork: No setup or content request exists unless the visitor confirms.
stages.evidenceRecovery: Cancel and pre-submit dismissal preserve local work without transmission.
stages.dataCrossing: Authorization precedes the content-free setup and the single content-bearing browser request for this attempt.
stages.failure: Authorization is absent, stale, or the component unmounts.
stages.recovery: Remain local and require a fresh deliberate action for any later attempt.

stages.visitorAction: Waits after the deliberate submission or cancels the client wait.
stages.frontstage: A finite working state is announced without promising success; a cookie, quota, or service failure requires another deliberate submission.
stages.backstage: Under one origin-wide Web Lock, the browser first sends a bodyless same-origin POST /api/lattice with Accept application/vnd.hah.text-to-lattice-visitor-session.v1+json and no Content-Type, then exactly one content POST whose body has text, requested_mode, and schema_version 1. A transport or non-204 setup response prevents that content POST. Because script cannot observe storage of the HttpOnly cookie, an accepted 204 setup may still be followed by the content POST when cookie storage was blocked or dropped. The Worker establishes or preserves the signed cookie without quota or provider work, rejects missing-cookie content as 428 visitor_session_required before admission or provider work, and rejects alternate origins, methods, paths, queries, media envelopes, shapes, modes, versions, oversized bodies, invalid or undeclared cookies, and account or provider credentials. After exact content validation and before provider work, it makes exactly one atomic claim against 30 accepted transformations globally per UTC day and 3 per cooperating canonical client with an ordinary persistent browser cookie jar per UTC day.
stages.supportNetwork: A first isolated setup has no Cookie header; its response sets only __Secure-hah-lattice-api-visitor with Path=/api/lattice, Secure, HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, no Domain, and expiry at the next UTC-day boundary. The following content request and later requests may carry only that signed opaque cookie. Setup consumes no transformation quota and makes no provider call. Each admitted attempt counts even after caller disconnect or provider failure, is not refunded, and receives no second shared quota check within its pipeline. At most 32 provider calls per admitted request yields at most 960 provider calls from admitted requests per UTC day; the 30-per-60-second path limiter remains an edge shaper. The API Worker also uses a 240-second request deadline, closed machine-readable errors, bounded Retry-After metadata, and Cache-Control: no-store.
stages.evidenceRecovery: A transport or non-204 setup failure prevents the content request and consumes no transformation quota. If a 204 setup's cookie is blocked or dropped, the Worker rejects the one content request before admission or provider work. Cancellation aborts the client wait but does not refund an admitted attempt; rate limit, timeout, invalid request, and service failures terminate without an automatic retry. Evidence retains only value-free cookie metadata.
stages.dataCrossing: The setup contains no submitted text. Only the content request places submitted text in bounded API request memory. HF_TOKEN and VISITOR_COOKIE_SECRET remain server-only; quota state contains only the current-day aggregate and bounded opaque visitor counts, never IP address, browser fingerprint, submitted content, or result; and no provider address or credential enters either browser request.
stages.failure: Setup transport or response fails, the signed cookie is blocked, dropped, or invalid, the content request is invalid, the global or scoped browser-cookie-jar UTC-day quota is exhausted, the admission authority or service fails closed, the client wait is canceled, the request times out, or the same-origin API is unreachable.
stages.recovery: Return a bounded error; setup or cookie-storage failure sends no content to the provider, any retry requires a new deliberate submission, and an admitted attempt remains counted without refund.

stages.visitorAction: Receives progress semantics only; cannot select a provider, URL, model, prompt, header, or credential.
stages.frontstage: The interface continues to describe external processing, not browser-local inference.
stages.backstage: The Worker creates bounded prompts, segments protected source spans, and uses the fixed Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507:nscale generator for atomization, classification, and planning; remote clarification remains disabled with questions required to be empty.
stages.supportNetwork: All stages use only https://router.huggingface.co/v1/chat/completions with their fixed Nscale-qualified role selector. Verification, its bounded correction and reverification, and certification use meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct:nscale with exact fitted strict JSON Schema response format and no tools or forced-tool selection. No automatic provider selection or fallback exists. Analysis, candidate, certification and repair calls have 120-second ceilings; verification has a 180-second ceiling; the authoritative 240-second whole-request deadline may end any stage sooner. Verification remains capped at 2,048 output tokens and certification at 520 within unchanged call and aggregate exposure limits.
stages.evidenceRecovery: Malformed, oversized, hostile, unavailable, or length-limited upstream output fails closed or receives only bounded same-model schema correction within the overall pipeline budget. A length finish is never prefix-parsed, silently completed, or automatically retried.
stages.dataCrossing: Server-created prompts containing submitted text cross to Hugging Face and Nscale; the browser never receives raw provider bodies.
stages.failure: The fixed generator times out, fails, or cannot produce an admissible closed record within budget.
stages.recovery: Terminate with a bounded error or unable-to-attempt outcome; do not switch provider or model.

stages.visitorAction: Waits for the bounded pipeline; no clarification question is presented.
stages.frontstage: The service does not solicit follow-up prose or silently broaden the requested mode.
stages.backstage: The fixed Qwen generator drafts a material candidate while deterministic checks enforce source coverage, protected spans, semantic polarity, quantities, modality, uncertainty, and bounded work and repair ceilings.
stages.supportNetwork: Schema correction and repair may call the same fixed generator within the declared completion budget, never as transport retry or provider/model fallback.
stages.evidenceRecovery: Rejected candidates and provider-authored issue prose cannot become new semantic authority.
stages.dataCrossing: Only bounded pipeline prompts and candidate records exist in request memory and provider processing; the application defines no persistent content sink.
stages.failure: No candidate clears the protected gates within the finite budget.
stages.recovery: Return unable-to-attempt with no transformed text or a bounded machine error.

stages.frontstage: The eventual label distinguishes translated, conformant-for-context, review-required, unable-to-attempt, and finite request errors.
stages.backstage: The fixed meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct:nscale verifier and deterministic validators independently check coverage, fidelity, accessibility, clarity, domain correctness, register fit, and ornament through closed structured-output contracts; verifier records cannot emit clarification questions. The host also carries an identity-owned same-passage D14 rewrite finding into normalized negative materiality before issue and decision consistency, so the existing bounded repair feedback reflects that known failure. It does not infer positive meaning or waive wire, grounding, structural or certification checks. A separate bounded recovery may repair an authentic D14 nonmaterial rewrite after unavailable initial verification only when the identity-owned terminal record is attempt 2 and both response-shape failures are wire-decoder/coverage V16M or V17M, with D14-only findings bound to current rewrite passages. The repair receives verification null rather than unavailable placeholder checks; it must earn fresh deterministic and full independent verification plus applicable certification. This uses the existing repair opportunity, never supplies missing support or positive semantic acceptance, and cannot be enabled by copied diagnostics, other failures, or mixed findings. Current v12 qualification diagnostics refine only an already-rejected passage failed-check width into V14LE (empty), V14LS (nonempty short) or V14LG (long), all wire-decoder/value-domain. Legacy V14L remains the undifferentiated width predicate for retained evidence. Existing identity-bound tuples carry these finite observations without raw masks, exact nonzero lengths, new fields or new headers. All variants retain the existing mask-width correction request and rejection behavior. No positive verification, new repair eligibility or release claim follows from a width observation.
stages.supportNetwork: Initial verification, bounded correction, reverification and certification use the unified https://router.huggingface.co/v1/chat/completions endpoint and fixed meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct:nscale selector. Each review stage sends its exact fitted closed schema using strict json_schema response_format, without tools or tool_choice, and accepts only one stopped assistant message with exactly role/content. Tool, legacy-function, auxiliary name/reasoning, unknown-field, incomplete-JSON and non-stop responses fail closed without channel or provider fallback. Verification has a 180-second call ceiling and 2,048 output tokens; certification has 120 seconds and 520 tokens; the authoritative 240-second whole-request deadline may end either sooner. The unchanged complete legal verifier bound is 1,326 pinned-tokenizer tokens and conservative certification bound 440. Public metadata supports the request contract but does not establish hosted grammar enforcement, serving identity or semantic success. Exact wire decoding and host validation remain mandatory. Both model roles now share Nscale; their independent role checks do not imply provider isolation.
stages.evidenceRecovery: Malformed, ambiguous, incomplete, or non-success responses including length finishes fail closed. Contract objects with undeclared fields fail closed. A verifier failure cannot be relabeled as success, prefix-parsed, automatically retried, or redirected to a provider or model fallback.
stages.dataCrossing: Verification prompts and candidate text cross the external-provider boundary in bounded request memory.
stages.failure: The candidate fails a semantic gate, the provider violates the closed structured-output contract, the completion ends at its bounded output limit, or deterministic host validation rejects the result.
stages.recovery: Bounded same-model repair may occur within policy; otherwise return review-required, unable-to-attempt, or a finite error as the closed protocol permits.

stages.phase: Return, retain locally, or start over
stages.visitorAction: Reads, copies, closes, starts over, or deliberately submits a later attempt.
stages.frontstage: The browser renders only the validated closed response, protects output interaction without claiming capture prevention, and exposes accurate retry timing without initiating it.
stages.backstage: The client rejects invalid, oversized, HTML, or non-JSON responses; terminal state remains local and reopenable while mounted, and teardown aborts active work.
stages.supportNetwork: API responses carry no-store; hah.dev defines no application database, object storage, cache, queue, raw-content log, or analytics event for content.
stages.evidenceRecovery: A new attempt requires a new explicit action. Repository checks do not prove live provider behavior or external-provider retention.
stages.dataCrossing: Bounded result or error returns to the browser; application request memory is released, while external-provider handling remains governed by its own policies.
stages.failure: The response is malformed, too large, interrupted, or the visitor dismisses during work.
stages.recovery: Show a bounded error or preserve valid terminal state; never auto-retry or route content elsewhere.

historicalBrowserLocalServiceBlueprint.scenario: A visitor converts authorized prose into one bounded Lattice outcome in the résumé demonstrator.
historicalBrowserLocalServiceBlueprint.actor: A visitor using a secure, JavaScript-capable browser with Unicode segmentation, WebGPU, and sufficient local storage.
historicalBrowserLocalServiceBlueprint.goal: Receive a materially revised, locally checked result; an unchanged context-bounded clearance; a review-marked draft; one precise clarification; or an honest refusal without transmitting prose to the lease service.
historicalBrowserLocalServiceBlueprint.methodNote: The blueprint follows NN/g's service-blueprint separation of user action, visible service, backstage process, and support process, then adds evidence and data-boundary rows because trust and recovery are part of this service.

lines.label: Line of interaction

lines.label: Line of visibility
lines.meaning: What is disclosed as status or outcome versus what remains internal pipeline work.

lines.label: Line of trust and network
lines.meaning: The only crossings are bounded attestation, lease metadata, and revision-pinned model assets; prose stays local.

lifecycleOwners.responsibility: Govern the method, licensed profile boundary, version, and authorized conformance claims.
lifecycleOwners.handoffEvidence: A cited upstream revision, applicable license terms, and an explicit public claim boundary.

lifecycleOwners.responsibility: Keep input, interaction, local pipeline, accessibility, privacy, teardown, and public outcome behavior aligned with the requirements.
lifecycleOwners.handoffEvidence: Exact source revision, automated contracts, manual interaction matrix, and built static artifact inspection.

lifecycleOwners.responsibility: Approve exact model, tokenizer, runtime, and WASM revisions plus their integrity, provenance, and license boundary.
lifecycleOwners.handoffEvidence: Pinned URLs and versions, tokenizer hashes, fetched artifact record, licenses, and a recorded disposition for the WASM provenance gap.

lifecycleOwners.responsibility: Operate request safety, secrets, signed credentials, exact admission, lifecycle accounting, alarms, retention, and fail-closed capacity policy; disclose whether the bounded testing or hostname-restricted attestation profile is active.
lifecycleOwners.handoffEvidence: Reviewed Worker revision, binding and secret-name inventory, exact authenticated route inventory, attestation-profile classification, provider metrics, and bounded load results.

lifecycleOwners.responsibility: Keep the dedicated static frame, origin policy, message protocol, CSP, provider action, and teardown boundary exact.
lifecycleOwners.handoffEvidence: Deployed header capture, route and origin inspection, protocol tests, provider hostname/action evidence, and accessibility exercise.

lifecycleOwners.handoffEvidence: Dated gate record naming the revision and artifact digests, with every open exception assigned or explicitly deferred.

lifecycleOwners.responsibility: Use text they are authorized to process, choose whether to download large local models, and decide whether the published device and provider residuals are acceptable.
lifecycleOwners.handoffEvidence: Visible purpose, size, privacy, capability, provider, outcome, and residual disclosures before consequential action.

stages.visitorAction: Opens Text to Lattice and reads the purpose, limits, privacy caution, and capability requirements.
stages.frontstage: The dialog names a local, bounded demonstration and keeps the canonical documentation path available.
stages.backstage: The interface probes secure context, Unicode segmentation, WebGPU, storage estimate, and cached-model state.
stages.supportNetwork: No service call and no model download occurs during source preflight or capability explanation.
stages.evidenceRecovery: Unsupported capability yields a precise unavailable state and preserves access to the semantic documentation page.
stages.dataCrossing: Capability metadata remains in the browser; no prose exists yet.
stages.failure: A browser cannot support the runtime or cannot establish a secure context.
stages.recovery: Read the method and limitation record; use a compatible browser or device without losing entered work.

stages.visitorAction: Enters one to 700 Unicode-aware words and chooses Convert.
stages.frontstage: The shared counter, inline validation, and concise status expose only actionable limits.
stages.backstage: The host validates control characters, Unicode structure, 12,000 code units, passage count, initial work groups, clarification limits, and completion ceilings before requesting capacity.
stages.supportNetwork: None; admission and model systems remain untouched until complete preflight succeeds.
stages.evidenceRecovery: The source stays editable. Rejection is local, bounded, and does not truncate or relabel text.
stages.dataCrossing: Source and structural findings stay in the browser document.
stages.failure: Input exceeds a published boundary or contains unsafe structure.
stages.recovery: Revise the source locally; no quota was consumed.

stages.visitorAction: Continues through the acquisition check when the service requires it.
stages.frontstage: A dedicated acquisition surface reports pending, interactive, completed, limited, or unavailable state; the demonstrable release discloses that Cloudflare's official testing profile supplies protocol exercise without anti-bot or availability assurance.
stages.backstage: An exact-origin guard rejects every browser origin other than https://hah.dev before any lease fetch. The official parent flow then creates a fresh correlation identifier, accepts only the exact frame origin and Window, and requests a lease with no request body.
stages.supportNetwork: In the official browser flow, the verify.hah.dev frame obtains the provider's public dummy token. The lease Worker accepts only that exact token with the matching official testing secret, requires Siteverify success, bounds the returned response timestamp, and then applies exact global admission, visitor eligibility, signing, and lease state. A direct caller can replay the public token without the frame; the profile provides no token-freshness, single-use, human-or-bot, hostname, or action assurance.
stages.evidenceRecovery: Acquisition, renewal, and release fetch plus response-body handling have a shared 30-second deadline; caller cancellation stays distinct from timeout. Bounded Retry-After values become a local retry ETA, and every terminal browser-flow path removes the frame and stale listeners. Local or Vite preview explains the canonical requirement without producing a missing local lease-route request.
stages.dataCrossing: Only closed acquisition messages, a token, request metadata, an opaque signed cookie, and lease credentials cross. Source, clarification, candidate, and output do not.
stages.failure: The browser origin is not canonical, acquisition rejects, the global or visitor budget is ineligible, or the support service is unavailable.
stages.recovery: Fail closed, show the canonical location, bounded reason, or ETA, and leave canonical documentation public; do not proxy or bypass the admission boundary.

stages.visitorAction: Waits while actual download or nondeterminate final-setup progress is announced, may dismiss and later return to the same work, or explicitly cancels.
stages.frontstage: The interface reports real generator or verifier download progress, becomes nondeterminate after the first completed WebLLM progress phase, stays nondeterminate across GPU-loading and shader-compilation resets, and never simulates delay or displays a stale full bar during later work.
stages.backstage: A dedicated worker proves its own WebGPU capability before lease acquisition, installs its network boundary before importing model libraries, validates closed RPC, acknowledges when each serialized request actually starts, loads one role at a time, and disables WebLLM's IndexedDB cache path. Per-operation deadlines begin at that acknowledgement, so a queued short request cannot terminate active work. Public model cache may remain and contains no prose.
stages.supportNetwork: Only manifest-enumerated, revision-pinned HTTPS model shards, tokenizers, and WASM assets may be requested with credentials omitted and no referrer.
stages.evidenceRecovery: Worker start is bounded to 30 seconds; preparation inactivity is 120 seconds, completion inactivity is 720 seconds, and 45-minute hard execution ceilings remain absolute. Phase-local progress resets count as liveness while duplicates do not postpone inactivity. The adapter check is bounded to 15 seconds, and the 10-second storage estimate degrades to unknown. Cancel interrupts generation, terminates the worker when necessary, and releases any acquired lease through bounded idempotent handling.
stages.dataCrossing: Pinned asset requests reveal ordinary network metadata and selected public model revisions; prose is not part of any URL, header, or asset body.
stages.failure: Worker start or worker-realm capability, storage, WebGPU, CORS, pinned assets, upstream availability, runtime preparation, or inference fails.
stages.recovery: Stop before lease acquisition when the worker realm is unsupported; otherwise unload local runtime, release capacity, and return an explicit unavailable result without candidate text.

stages.visitorAction: Reads bounded progress; no additional action is required unless ambiguity is material.
stages.frontstage: Status names analysis rather than claiming completion.
stages.backstage: Lossless passages are serialized as inert JSON, analyzed without clarification history, schema-checked, host-normalized, and checked against evidence spans and context budgets. Each SHA-256 provenance binding has a 10-second browser deadline.
stages.supportNetwork: No support service receives model prompts or prose; inference runs inside the browser worker.
stages.evidenceRecovery: Malformed, oversized, mismatched, or under-evidenced analysis is rejected before it can authorize drafting. An unavailable or stalled browser digest fails explicitly rather than leaving processing pending.
stages.dataCrossing: Source crosses the document-to-worker boundary through closed RPC; it does not cross the browser network boundary.
stages.failure: A provenance digest stalls, or the model cannot return a complete, closed, evidence-linked analysis within fixed budgets.
stages.recovery: Return unable-to-attempt, or ask one provenance-bound clarification when the analyzer identifies a resolvable ambiguity.

stages.visitorAction: Answers one short, enumerated clarification when asked, or continues waiting for a draft.
stages.frontstage: The interface exposes only a precise host-normalized question and bounded answer controls; candidate text remains hidden.
stages.backstage: One exact matching answer authorizes one analyzer recheck. The generator drafts a material candidate subject to protected spans, semantic obligations, word materiality, and fixed completion budgets.
stages.supportNetwork: Lease renewal may extend bounded capacity; its request carries the credential but no prose.
stages.evidenceRecovery: A repeated question cannot become acceptance. A draft that merely changes punctuation, casing, or spacing is not material.
stages.dataCrossing: Clarification and draft remain inside the browser and local worker; renewal metadata alone crosses the network.
stages.failure: Ambiguity remains, provenance mismatches, or no material candidate can be produced safely.
stages.recovery: Return needs-clarification or unable-to-attempt without exposing a candidate-dependent trace.

stages.visitorAction: Waits through explicit verification and bounded repair states.
stages.frontstage: The interface reports checking, repair, or certification without presenting rejected work as a result.
stages.backstage: A distinct verifier model, deterministic validators, post-candidate re-atomization, bounded repair, and whole-document certification test fidelity, coverage, domain correctness, accessibility, clarity, register fit, and materiality.
stages.supportNetwork: No verifier finding, atom identifier, candidate, or certification record leaves the browser.
stages.evidenceRecovery: Rejected candidates are withheld. The public projection removes candidate-dependent identifiers, counts, layers, and issue categories.
stages.dataCrossing: Candidate data crosses only the closed document-to-worker boundary; support services receive no semantic content.
stages.failure: A release gate fails, budgets exhaust, or a lower-priority issue remains.
stages.recovery: Repair within fixed ceilings; otherwise return review-required when semantically releasable or unable-to-attempt with one host-authored record.

stages.visitorAction: Reads the outcome, dismisses and later returns to the same input, request, process, clarification, error, or result, or explicitly cancels or starts over.
stages.frontstage: The interface presents exactly one outcome state, explicit limitation, and protected result region; it never calls review-required complete clearance. A visible Close action, backdrop, and Escape are visibility-only in every phase while the résumé remains mounted.
stages.backstage: Ordinary dismissal preserves input, availability or attestation request, lease-bound conversion, post-request processing, clarification, error, terminal state, and result for reopening. Cancel and Start over terminate or reset the current request, and component unmount tears it down; completion and error may release runtime resources, but their terminal state remains reopenable; output remains transient and is concealed on blur, page invisibility, print, and detectable Print Screen events.
stages.supportNetwork: Ordinary dismissal does not release an opaque lease or abort an in-flight acquisition or attestation. Completion, explicit cancellation, or teardown releases capacity with bounded idempotent retries; the global authority updates lifecycle state and expiry alarms.
stages.evidenceRecovery: Reopening restores the same mounted request and state in every phase. A release failure remains bounded and retryable. Static HTML, Markdown, JSON, JSON-LD, sitemap, and llms surfaces remain available when the service fails closed.
stages.dataCrossing: Release credentials and operation identifiers may cross; result text stays transient in browser memory and is never sent to the lease service or static evidence surfaces.
stages.failure: Output capture cannot be fully prevented, focus must be restored safely when hidden work is reopened, release can race unload, or the remote authority can be unavailable.
stages.recovery: Preserve mounted work across ordinary dismissal; focus the active attestation, Cancel, clarification, result, or source when reopened; tear down the current request only through Cancel, Start over, or component unmount; keep completion and error reopenable; and retain lease expiry as the final backstop. Documentation states that browser, operating-system, camera, and assistive-technology capture cannot be guaranteed away.

securityModel.scope: Threat model for the active hah.dev Text to Lattice remote capability: deliberate browser submission, content-free visitor-session setup and one content request under the same origin-wide Web Lock, same-origin API validation, fixed server-side Hugging Face and Nscale processing, bounded response handling, and application-level nonretention. Historical WebLLM, Turnstile, and lease controls are inactive and cannot satisfy this model.
securityModel.method: Prioritize controls where consequence, realistic plausibility, and lifecycle reuse are jointly high. Preserve uncomfortable residuals: probabilistic semantic drift, external-provider processing and retention, public-endpoint abuse, output capture, supply-chain change, and the gap between source checks and production evidence.

assets.label: Visitor source, prompts, candidates, and results
assets.objective: Confidentiality, integrity, exact transmission authorization, and no application persistence.

assets.label: Semantic obligations and outcome labels
assets.objective: Coverage, polarity, modality, quantity, uncertainty, ordering, accessibility, and honest withholding.

assets.label: Named browser capability and provider credential
assets.objective: Exact same-origin request construction and server-only HF_TOKEN secrecy.

assets.label: Provider budget and service availability
assets.objective: Bounded request, provider-call, completion, response-size, and retry behavior under public traffic.

assets.label: Endpoint, provider, model, schema, and prompt integrity
assets.objective: Fixed routing and roles without user-selected targets, silent substitution, or fallback.

assets.label: Public disclosures and release evidence
assets.objective: Traceability to exact source and deployed behavior without overstating privacy, accessibility, anti-abuse, or conformance.

trustBoundaries.label: Visitor prose and browser UI
trustBoundaries.crossing: Untrusted authorized prose becomes inert local state; only an explicit external-processing action may authorize transmission.

trustBoundaries.label: Browser and same-origin /api/lattice
trustBoundaries.crossing: After explicit confirmation, one bodyless setup establishes or preserves the signed cookie without quota or provider work; under the same Web Lock exactly one content POST carries text, requested_mode, and schema_version 1. The browser accepts only bounded closed success or error envelopes.

trustBoundaries.label: API Worker and Hugging Face router
trustBoundaries.crossing: Server-created prompts cross only to the fixed chat-completions endpoint with a server-only credential and fixed Nscale-served generator and Nscale-served verifier roles.

trustBoundaries.label: Bounded request memory and persistence surfaces
trustBoundaries.crossing: Source, prompts, candidates, results, and raw provider bodies may exist transiently in request memory but have no application database, object store, cache, queue, raw-content log, or analytics sink.

trustBoundaries.label: Provider response and public result
trustBoundaries.crossing: Closed structured output, deterministic fail-closed host validation, size ceilings, and text-only rendering separate untrusted provider output from public outcome claims.

trustBoundaries.label: Source register and generated documentation
trustBoundaries.crossing: Escaped deterministic projections expose current claims and clearly marked historical evidence but no visitor content, secrets, or private profile inventory.

threats.title: Content is transmitted without valid authorization or to an undeclared destination
threats.vector: Open, edit, validation, prefetch, cancellation, implicit submit, setup failure, blocked cookie storage, automatic retry, a user-controlled target, or a client-visible provider call sends content before deliberate confirmation or outside the named path.
threats.consequence: Sensitive text leaves the browser contrary to the visitor's choice and the public disclosure.
threats.plausibility: Ordinary UI, transport, and configuration regressions can create premature, duplicate, or misdirected requests.
threats.lifecycleValue: One named capability and one explicit-action boundary remain reusable across interface and provider revisions.
threats.classificationRationale: Unauthorized or misdirected disclosure is high consequence, integration-plausible, and cheaply prevented by exact request construction and deployment probes.
asBuilt: The browser capability is fixed to same-origin POST /api/lattice. Under one origin-wide Web Lock it sends a content-free visitor-session setup followed by exactly one content request containing text, requested_mode, and schema_version 1.

Open, edit, validation failure, pre-submit dismissal, and cancellation create no setup or transformation request; a transport or non-204 setup failure prevents the content request; if an accepted setup's HttpOnly cookie is blocked or dropped, the Worker rejects the content request before admission or provider work; terminal failures do not automatically retry.
The Worker alone calls the fixed Hugging Face endpoint and fixed Nscale-served generator and Nscale-served verifier identifiers.
requiredBeforePublication: Verify zero network requests before explicit submission on the exact deployed artifact.

Capture one successful deployed sequence and the accepted-setup/cookie-blocked failure path; confirm the setup is content-free, exactly one content request follows an accepted setup under the same lock, and the browser contacts only same-origin /api/lattice while Worker egress remains fixed.
residualBoundary: The authorized content request necessarily transmits content to Hugging Face, Nscale, and their infrastructure.
Browser extensions, security software, DNS, networks, and provider infrastructure remain outside hah.dev control.

threats.title: Hostile prose or provider output acquires authority or execution
threats.vector: Prompt injection, control characters, bidi abuse, HTML-like content, or provider-authored issue text becomes an instruction, executable markup, semantic authority, or generated-document markup.
threats.consequence: The pipeline can ignore its contract, misrepresent a finding, execute injected content, or expose unsafe markup.
threats.plausibility: Directly plausible because arbitrary prose and probabilistic provider output are intended inputs.
threats.lifecycleValue: Inert serialization, closed schemas, host-authored public fields, and text-only rendering protect future model and document revisions.
threats.classificationRationale: The input and provider boundaries are necessarily hostile, so containment is a primary release condition.
asBuilt: Complete Unicode and structural preflight occurs before the provider pipeline.

System instructions are separated from serialized user data. Verification requests a dedicated JSON-object assistant content channel without tools or tool_choice, and accepts only stop-finished content under its minimal envelope guard: absent tool_calls or an independently opted-in empty array or literal null, no legacy function_call, and the metadata fields name and reasoning_content only when literally null. The literal-null collection exception is enabled only for this exact dedicated verifier JSON-object channel following actual S02N evidence. A nonempty tool collection, every other nonarray collection, non-null metadata or any other extra field is rejected; neither message nor content is rewritten. Certification retains one exact named call as authoritative or its explicitly enabled minimal stopped assistant envelope with absent tool fields or an empty tool_calls array, without the verification-only null metadata allowance. Generic defaults are unchanged. Bounded complete JSON and exact fitted closed decoding and host semantics remain mandatory; auxiliary provider prose is never interpreted.
Public issue categories are host-controlled and React and documentation generators escape untrusted text.
requiredBeforePublication: Re-run injection, Unicode, recursive noninterference, malformed-provider-response, and documentation-escaping checks on the release artifact.
Review any new renderer, logging hook, response transport, compatibility path, or model transport for HTML interpretation or dynamic authority.
residualBoundary: A fixed model can still misunderstand inert data; later semantic gates contain but cannot eliminate that risk.

threats.title: Semantic drift is released as success
threats.vector: Generation drops, invents, negates, broadens, narrows, or reorders a material obligation and a correlated checker accepts the candidate.
threats.consequence: Safety instructions, conditions, quantities, uncertainty, causality, consequences, or recovery relationships change while the interface claims success.
threats.plausibility: Probabilistic server-side generation makes drift realistic even with structured output.
threats.lifecycleValue: A distinct verifier, deterministic sentinels, source-grounded reanalysis, and honest withholding remain useful across provider revisions.
threats.classificationRationale: Meaning preservation is the product's central consequence; incorrect success is worse than refusal.
asBuilt: Protected spans and semantic sentinels preserve explicit high-consequence content.

Fixed Qwen generation is checked by fixed Llama verification, deterministic validators, source-grounded reanalysis, bounded repair, and whole-document certification. An identity-owned D14 finding for the same passage under a rewrite plan sets normalized materiality to false before verifier issue and decision consistency. The host supplies a binding negative from its existing deterministic check, never positive semantic acceptance. This negative is carried into the existing bounded repair feedback. Unowned, cloned, other-passage and retained-plan findings cannot supply it; unsupported contradictions without D14 still fail closed. A copied repair remains withheld, and a material repair still requires independent reverification and applicable certification. A restored D14 candidate may consequently receive the existing semantic-rejection held diagnostic category; that classification supplies no public success claim. A separate bounded recovery may repair an authentic D14 nonmaterial rewrite after unavailable initial verification only when the identity-owned terminal record is attempt 2 and both response-shape failures are wire-decoder/coverage V16M or V17M, with D14-only findings bound to current rewrite passages. The repair receives verification null rather than unavailable placeholder checks; it must earn fresh deterministic and full independent verification plus applicable certification. This uses the existing repair opportunity, never supplies missing support or positive semantic acceptance, and cannot be enabled by copied diagnostics, other failures, or mixed findings. Current v12 qualification diagnostics refine only an already-rejected passage failed-check width into V14LE (empty), V14LS (nonempty short) or V14LG (long), all wire-decoder/value-domain. Legacy V14L remains the undifferentiated width predicate for retained evidence. Existing identity-bound tuples carry these finite observations without raw masks, exact nonzero lengths, new fields or new headers. All variants retain the existing mask-width correction request and rejection behavior. No positive verification, new repair eligibility or release claim follows from a width observation.
Five outcome states prevent withheld or unresolved work from being relabeled as complete; remote clarification is disabled.
requiredBeforePublication: Run the full adversarial and semantic regression corpus against the exact remote release revisions.
Record manual review across realistic genres without treating samples as universal proof.
residualBoundary: No bounded corpus or fixed model pair proves equivalence for all prose.
Review-required is semantically releasable but explicitly not complete bounded clearance.

threats.title: Input or remote inference exhausts bounded resources
threats.vector: Pathological Unicode, oversized JSON, dense passages, excessive completions, stalled provider calls, repair loops, oversized responses, repeated ordinary-browser use, or distributed valid requests consume bounded browser, Worker, provider, or account resources.
threats.consequence: The interaction hangs, legitimate visitors exhaust the exact daily admission, provider spend exceeds the intended demonstration budget, or a response exceeds safe client handling.
threats.plausibility: Realistic for arbitrary public input and third-party inference.
threats.lifecycleValue: Atomic daily admission, centralized ceilings, identity minimization, and fail-closed deadlines bound future pipeline stages and provider revisions.
threats.classificationRationale: Public arbitrary input and paid external work make resource exhaustion ordinary and consequential; an exact global cap has high value even though a cookie-jar limit cannot identify a person.

threats.title: Endpoint, provider, model, schema, or dependency identity drifts

threats.plausibility: Hosted model and dependency services can change independently of repository source even when identifiers are fixed.
threats.lifecycleValue: Exact endpoint and model allowlists plus requalification rules scale across upgrades and incidents.
threats.classificationRationale: Silent substitution affects both semantic and data-processing claims; fixed targets and explicit requalification have high marginal value.
asBuilt: The adapter fixes https://router.huggingface.co/v1/chat/completions for every stage with Qwen/Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507:nscale for generation and meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct:nscale for verification and certification. No active DeepInfra proxy or mapped request-model override remains.
User content cannot determine a URL, provider, model, header, or credential, and no provider or model fallback exists.

No tools, forced-tool selection, auxiliary review fields or alternate output channel are enabled. residualBoundary: Provider-managed serving is not byte-equivalent to the historical MLC artifacts and no such claim is made.

threats.plausibility: Routine for a public HTTP endpoint and easy to automate.
threats.lifecycleValue: Two closed fail-closed HTTP envelopes on one named capability remain reusable regardless of provider implementation.
threats.classificationRationale: The probes are low-cost and directly protect privacy, cost, and protocol integrity.
asBuilt: The API accepts same-origin POST /api/lattice only as the bodyless custom-Accept visitor-session setup or the exact closed JSON content body.

Origin, path, query, method, body presence, content length, Accept, Content-Type, cookie, word count, mode, version, and keys fail closed before provider use; missing-cookie content returns 428 before admission or provider use.
Success and error envelopes are exact, bounded, and no-store.

Confirm rejected probes and every setup request create no provider call, and setup creates no quota claim.

Infrastructure before the Worker may still process ordinary connection metadata.

threats.title: Application storage, logging, caching, queues, or analytics retain content
threats.vector: A database binding, object store, cache, service worker, raw request or provider log, exception report, background queue, analytics event, or edge transformation captures content.
threats.consequence: Source or derived text persists beyond the request and contradicts the application no-retention claim.
threats.plausibility: Telemetry and convenience logging are ordinary service-development regressions.
threats.lifecycleValue: A sink inventory, no-store policy, and content-free observability rule protect every future endpoint revision.
threats.classificationRationale: Persistence is high consequence and preventable within the application boundary, while external-provider behavior must remain a disclosed limitation.

Ordinary and expired responses omit these diagnostics; the canary rejects partial or inconsistent groups. No new content retention or logging is introduced. Current v12 qualification diagnostics refine only an already-rejected passage failed-check width into V14LE (empty), V14LS (nonempty short) or V14LG (long), all wire-decoder/value-domain. Existing identity-bound tuples carry these finite observations without raw masks, exact nonzero lengths, new fields or new headers. All variants retain the existing mask-width correction request and rejection behavior. No positive verification, new repair eligibility or release claim follows from a width observation.
The API configuration defines no application database, object storage, cache, or queue for content.
The Worker and adapter do not emit raw-content logs or analytics and return Cache-Control: no-store.
The browser excludes /api/lattice from service-worker or cache interception under the named capability contract.

Run a sanitized trace and log review using unique non-sensitive markers without claiming control of provider retention.
residualBoundary: Hugging Face, Nscale, and their infrastructure handle content and connection metadata under their own policies.
No application-retention statement proves deletion or retention behavior inside an external provider.

residualBoundary: Screenshots, cameras, privileged extensions, developer tools, and memory access remain possible.

prePublicationGates.label: Remote provider capacity and cost boundary
prePublicationGates.requirement: The bodyless visitor-session setup must make no quota claim and no provider call. A content request with no cookie must fail 428 visitor_session_required, while one with an invalid, tampered, or undeclared cookie must fail 403 invalid_request, before Durable Object admission or provider work in either case. After exact content-request validation and before provider work, the deployed API must make exactly one atomic admission claim and accept at most 30 transformations globally per UTC day and 3 per cooperating canonical client with an ordinary persistent browser cookie jar per UTC day. Intentional cookie clearing and uncooperative callers remain outside the per-browser identity claim; the global 30-per-day counter remains exact and authoritative. An admitted attempt counts even if its caller disconnects or provider work later fails; it is never refunded and encounters no second shared quota claim within its pipeline. Quota identity and state use no IP address, browser fingerprint, submitted content, or result. Each admitted request permits at most 32 provider calls, so admitted requests expose at most 960 provider calls per UTC day. The path-scoped Worker rate limiter remains a 30-per-60-second edge shaper. Analysis, candidate, certification, and repair calls must each be bounded to 120 seconds, verification to 180 seconds, and the authoritative whole request to 240 seconds so it may end any stage sooner; response size remains bounded, with no paid or generic proxy path and no promise of provider rate, retention, availability, or cost behavior.
prePublicationGates.currentEvidence: Deterministic source contracts bound per-visitor and global admission, lease lifetime, retry behavior, row lifecycle, and fail-closed provider errors. Under the public reusable testing token, however, one client can use the permitted 16-request acquisition sequence to fill all eight slots and renew them; the 48-per-10-second per-IP rule does not stop that sequence. The controls bound cost, state, and privacy consequence, not tool availability, and source cannot establish live provider capacity.

Prove that visitor-session setup and preservation make no quota claim or provider call, missing-cookie content fails 428 visitor_session_required, invalid, tampered, or undeclared-cookie content fails 403 invalid_request before admission or provider work, and one claim occurs per exactly validated content request. Prove 30 accepted transformations globally per UTC day, 3 per cooperating canonical client with an ordinary persistent browser cookie jar per UTC day, UTC-day rollover, count-on-admission without refund after disconnect or provider failure, and no second shared quota claim within an admitted pipeline. Record intentional cookie clearing and uncooperative callers outside the per-browser identity claim while proving the exact global counter remains authoritative. Confirm quota identity and state contain no IP address, browser fingerprint, submitted content, or result; record the 32-provider-call per-admission ceiling and resulting 960-call maximum daily provider exposure; record bounded production-representative timeout, rate-limit, malformed-response, latency, and cost behavior; confirm no generic proxy or paid fallback path; and record external provider retention and availability as unguaranteed. Retain observed abuse or cost drift as a requalification trigger.
prePublicationGates.rationale: A public content-bearing endpoint can multiply model calls and cost even when application storage is absent. The exact global admission cap authoritatively bounds accepted work even when a caller clears or partitions the ordinary-browser quota cookie, while the browser limit still reduces ordinary repeated use. A missing or non-atomic production binding, quota or UTC-rollover drift, refund or in-pipeline recheck, identity expansion, provider-bound mismatch, or generic escape path would be consequential. This gate stays open until the deployed boundary is observed.
