threats.title: Prose crosses a network boundary
threats.vector: A URL, header, request body, telemetry hook, attestation message, or error report incorporates source, clarification, candidate, or result text.
threats.consequence: Private or sensitive prose leaves the visitor's browser and contradicts the core privacy claim.
threats.plausibility: Realistic whenever a model runtime, verification provider, or usage service performs network work.
threats.lifecycleValue: A single enforced data-flow boundary is reusable across every pipeline stage and dependency revision.
threats.classificationRationale: High consequence, ordinary integration plausibility, and architectural reuse require source controls plus immediate post-deployment trace verification and a hard disable condition.
asBuilt: The official lease acquisition has no request body and the published policy forbids source transmission.
Model asset URLs and headers are constant, enumerated, credentialless, and independent of user content.
The attestation protocol uses closed messages without source or output.
The reviewed first-session canonical-client evidence records Safari/WebKit and Brave/Chromium lifecycle behavior plus a capture-wide zero-match source-marker review across hah.dev and verify.hah.dev.
requiredBeforePublication: Keep the bodyless lease, closed attestation schema, local inference, and content-telemetry prohibition machine-bound in the qualified source set.

Retain the completed first-activation-session supported-browser trace and repeat it after consequential changes; the machine transition still sets GATE-06 to open-release-blocker and restores the held client when any content-bearing request appears.
residualBoundary: IP address, user agent, timing, public model choice, and ordinary transport metadata remain visible to contacted providers.
The repository test suite is not a capture of deployed traffic.

Cloudflare's edge-injected Web Analytics tag remains visible in the reviewed HTML response, but CSP blocked the external beacon resource before transfer or execution and no RUM submission was observed; this does not establish that Web Analytics is disabled or remove ordinary provider transport metadata.

threats.title: Hostile prose acquires authority or execution
threats.vector: Prompt injection, control characters, bidi abuse, HTML-like content, or model-authored issue text becomes an instruction, executable markup, or public authority.
threats.consequence: The pipeline can ignore its contract, misrepresent a finding, execute injected content, or expose unsafe markup.
threats.plausibility: Directly plausible because arbitrary prose is the intended input.
threats.lifecycleValue: Inert serialization and text-only rendering protect every future model and document revision.
threats.classificationRationale: The input channel is necessarily hostile, so containment is a primary release boundary.
asBuilt: Complete Unicode and structural preflight precedes lease acquisition and model load.
System instructions are separated from escaped JSON user data and constrained by closed schemas.
Public findings are host-authored and React renders visitor and model text as text nodes.
requiredBeforePublication: Re-run injection, Unicode, recursive noninterference, and generated-document escaping checks on the release artifact.
Review any new renderer or model transport for HTML interpretation or dynamic authority.
residualBoundary: A local model can still misunderstand inert data; later release gates, not prompt wording alone, contain that risk.

threats.title: Semantic drift is released as success
threats.vector: Generation drops, invents, negates, broadens, narrows, or reorders a material obligation and a correlated checker accepts the candidate.
threats.consequence: Safety instructions, conditions, quantities, uncertainty, causality, consequences, or recovery relationships can change while the interface claims successful transformation.
threats.plausibility: Probabilistic generation makes drift realistic even under structured output.
threats.lifecycleValue: Independent verification, deterministic sentinels, and honest withholding remain useful across model upgrades.
threats.classificationRationale: Meaning preservation is the product's central consequence; an incorrect success is worse than a refusal.
asBuilt: Protected spans and semantic sentinels preserve explicit high-consequence content.
A distinct verifier, deterministic validators, re-atomization, repair, and whole-document certification gate release.
Five outcome states prevent withheld or unresolved work from being relabeled as complete.
requiredBeforePublication: Run the full adversarial and semantic regression corpus against exact release revisions.
Record manual review across realistic genres without treating those samples as universal proof.
residualBoundary: No bounded corpus or model pair proves equivalence for all prose.
Review-required is semantically releasable but explicitly not complete bounded clearance.

threats.title: Input or inference exhausts browser resources
threats.vector: Pathological Unicode, dense passages, oversized tokens, retry subdivision, completion loops, worker queues, or memory pressure trigger unbounded local work.
threats.consequence: The page stalls, a device becomes unstable, accessibility degrades, or capacity remains occupied without useful work.
threats.plausibility: Realistic for arbitrary prose and multi-gigabyte browser models, especially on constrained devices.
threats.lifecycleValue: Central ceilings and early preflight bound new pipeline stages as the implementation evolves.
threats.classificationRationale: Common resource variability and meaningful reliability consequences justify fixing and testing the boundary now.
asBuilt: Word, code-unit, grapheme, token, control, passage, batch, executed-group, context, completion, queue, and response ceilings are explicit.

Preflight completes before lease or model load. A closed worker-start acknowledgement begins execution deadlines only when serialized work starts; 30-second start, 120-second preparation-inactivity, 720-second completion-inactivity, and 45-minute absolute execution bounds terminate stalls explicitly.

WebLLM download, GPU-loading, and shader-compilation resets are treated as distinct live phases; after the first completed phase the interface remains nondeterminate, and duplicate progress cannot slide inactivity.
Each SHA-256 provenance binding has a 10-second browser deadline and fails explicitly when secure digest support is unavailable or stalled.
requiredBeforePublication: Measure representative supported devices for memory, storage, cancellation, thermal load, and worst-case completion time.
Verify deployed limits match the documented constants after bundling.
residualBoundary: WebGPU drivers and browser memory management remain outside application control.
A supported capability probe cannot guarantee stable inference on every device.

threats.title: Pinned supply-chain artifact is substituted or lacks usable provenance
threats.vector: A model shard, tokenizer, WASM binary, runtime package, CDN response, or upstream license changes, is substituted, or cannot be related to a licensed source build.
threats.consequence: Inference semantics, code execution, availability, incident response, or redistribution authority can diverge from the reviewed build.
threats.plausibility: Revision and digest pinning lower accidental drift, but executable third-party binaries and incomplete build custody remain realistic dependencies.
threats.lifecycleValue: One artifact identity and qualification record scales across upgrades, audits, and incident response.
threats.classificationRationale: Untreated executable substitution is high consequence, so exact identity and runtime-integrity controls are high-value fixes. The remaining source-equivalence, build-custody, and artifact-authorization record is a distinct moderate accepted residual; hashes do not cure that custody gap.
asBuilt: Models, runtime versions, tokenizer and WASM hashes, WASM repository commit, current binary blobs, upstream PR 158, and the named TVM and MLC-LLM source commits are recorded.

The worker installs its request and cache policies before loading model modules: the exact two WASM and two tokenizer requests enforce SRI, protected Cache API hits are SHA-256 checked and mismatches are evicted before use, and allowed shards stay bounded to immutable model-revision URLs.
The release workflow independently verifies pinned WASM identities, while the public bundle excludes the runtime whenever a release blocker is open.
requiredBeforePublication: Fetch and compare the pinned tokenizer and WASM byte identities through the authorized release workflow.
Keep the incomplete Llama conversion narrative and WASM reproducibility and notice custody explicit as accepted residual risks; do not imply a source-equivalent rebuild.
Requalify any artifact, runtime, repository, digest, ABI, configuration, or terms change before publication.
residualBoundary: Upstream PR 158 establishes source-commit lineage for the current WASM files, not byte-reproducible compilation or a standalone binary-repository license grant.
A source pin or binary hash alone does not prove source equivalence, compiler behavior, dependency completeness, or redistribution authority.

threats.title: Cross-origin attestation is forged, replayed, or confused
threats.vector: A sibling frame, mismatched production hostname/action, guessed correlation identifier, unexpected message shape, or replayed public demonstration token reaches grant accounting.
threats.consequence: Automated or cross-site traffic can consume scarce capacity or bind a real-profile verification to the wrong visitor flow.
threats.plausibility: Cross-origin messaging and bearer tokens create a routine web attack surface; the bounded official testing profile intentionally publishes a reusable token and provides no bot discrimination.
threats.lifecycleValue: A closed versioned browser protocol, explicit credential profiles, and signed lease boundary remain reusable if the provider or frame changes.
threats.classificationRationale: Origin, message, and signed-lease checks protect realistic browser and credential-integrity boundaries. The demonstration token's replayability remains a moderate accepted availability residual for this capacity-capped portfolio tool, not an exotic edge case; a real hostname-restricted profile is required before claiming token freshness, single use, or anti-bot protection.
asBuilt: The official parent flow checks exact origin, exact Window source, protocol version, closed keys, and a fresh 144-bit correlation identifier.

Under the demonstration profile, the server accepts only the exact published dummy token with the exact testing secret, requires Siteverify success, and bounds the returned response timestamp; it does not claim token freshness, single use, frame participation, human-or-bot verification, hostname, or action assurance.

A real profile additionally requires hostname and action while the provider enforces its token rules. Exact admission and signed lease state remain downstream in either profile; every terminal official-browser path removes the frame.
requiredBeforePublication: For GATE-02, verify deployed frame bytes and headers, exact origin routing, the advertised testing site key, invalid-token rejection, and a bodyless dummy-token Siteverify, acquisition, and release API round trip; do not call that browser or frame proof.
Keep the official testing profile visibly classified as demonstration-only, and replace and requalify it before claiming production anti-bot protection.

Retain the reviewed official browser flow and two-origin privacy trace as historical evidence for its deployed revision, and repeat the functional conversion, lifecycle, and privacy evidence under GATE-06 after consequential changes; continue keyboard and assistive-technology verification under GATE-05.
residualBoundary: A direct caller can skip the frame and replay the official testing token; the profile does not distinguish people from automated clients or assure availability.
Provider availability, accessibility, fraud scoring, and privacy practices remain external dependencies.

threats.title: Lease or accounting state is abused
threats.vector: Forged, expired, replayed, cross-method, cross-owner, concurrently mutated, or indefinitely stalled credentials and responses cause duplicate grants, stolen renewals, missed releases, or inconsistent counts.
threats.consequence: One visitor can monopolize capacity, legitimate work can be denied, or the global authority can drift from real lifecycle state.
threats.plausibility: Any public signed-credential lifecycle is exposed to replay, concurrency races, and transport stalls.
threats.lifecycleValue: Exact state transitions and one global authority simplify every future quota policy.
threats.classificationRationale: Shared capacity depends on exact lifecycle integrity under ordinary concurrency and hostile replay.
asBuilt: Distinct HMAC secrets bind visitor cookies and lease credentials; canonical encoding, expiry, method, and actor checks precede state work.
One globally named SQLite-backed Durable Object serializes exact admissions, grants, renewals, releases, ownership, and expiry.

Acquisition, renewal, and release share a 30-second fetch-and-bounded-body deadline; caller AbortError remains distinct, stalled bodies are canceled without awaiting an uncooperative cancel promise, and release failure settles false.
requiredBeforePublication: Deploy with independent encrypted secrets and exercise concurrent production transitions, alarm recovery, and secret rotation.
Confirm idempotent client release behavior against deployed Retry-After variants and stalled response bodies.
residualBoundary: Provider point-in-time recovery may retain pseudonymous state for the published recovery window.
Network loss can leave a lease until bounded expiry even when local teardown succeeds.

threats.title: Automated or distributed traffic exhausts capacity
threats.vector: One caller replays the public testing token through sixteen acquisition requests to occupy all eight slots, or distributed callers invoke the public Worker before in-Worker shaping and exceed accounting assumptions.
threats.consequence: The demonstrator becomes unavailable to legitimate visitors or consumes shared free-tier capacity; other static evidence must remain available.
threats.plausibility: Realistic and easy under the disclosed testing profile. The 48-request-per-10-second IP rule would not stop the sixteen-request slot acquisition, and location-local permissive counters cannot guarantee an aggregate Worker-invocation ceiling.
threats.lifecycleValue: Separating exact downstream accounting, honest availability claims, and best-effort edge shedding prevents false capacity claims in later deployments.
threats.classificationRationale: The threat is consequential and plausible. Exact global admission and expiry bound its blast radius to tool availability and free-tier work but do not make the attacker unlikely. For this explicitly capacity-capped portfolio demonstrator, accepting that availability residual has moderate incremental release cost only with prominent disclosure, rollback on observed abuse, and requalification before any operational anti-bot claim.
asBuilt: Exact global minute and UTC-day admission precedes Siteverify and lifecycle work; visitor, grant, and active-lease caps bound downstream resources but do not prevent a caller from minting multiple visitor cookies.
Ingress, method, path, and credential shapers shed local load, while policy states they do not guarantee billed invocation limits or stop the sixteen-request slot-starvation sequence.
Quota exhaustion fails closed, the UI promises no availability assurance, and static semantic pages remain unrestricted.
requiredBeforePublication: Disclose the concrete eight-slot starvation path and that the bounded testing profile offers no anti-bot or availability assurance.
Treat the path-scoped 48-request-per-10-second IP rule as recommended GATE-03 operational hardening, not proof against slot starvation; record it and provider capacity measurements when available.
Replace and requalify the testing profile before claiming anti-bot protection, and restore the held client if observed abuse defeats demonstrable use.
residualBoundary: One client can fill and renew all eight slots with the reusable public token; the documented IP rule does not stop the acquisition sequence.
The Cloudflare Free plan does not provide an exact in-application bound on hostile Worker invocations, and distributed traffic remains outside the deterministic budget proof.

threats.title: Generated output is captured despite interface friction
threats.vector: Selection APIs, clipboard events, printing, page capture, browser extensions, developer tools, accessibility APIs, operating-system screenshots, cameras, or memory inspection obtain result text.
threats.consequence: A visitor or third party retains output despite the interface's deterrent treatment, and an overstated claim would mislead users about control.
threats.plausibility: Browser event controls can block routine paths, but privileged and out-of-band capture is always plausible.
threats.lifecycleValue: An honest limitation prevents future styling or browser changes from becoming a false security promise.
threats.classificationRationale: The privacy consequence is meaningful, but bespoke escalation cannot close the browser and operating-system boundary; the bounded fix is deterrence plus precise disclosure.
asBuilt: Routine selection, copy, cut, drag, context menu, touch callout, and print paths are disabled for generated output.
Visibility, blur, print, and detectable Print Screen events conceal output behind a reduced-motion-compatible veil.
Semantic access is preserved and the canonical limitation rejects guarantees of capture prevention or AI unreadability.
requiredBeforePublication: Manually exercise keyboard, touch, print, visibility, blur, reduced-motion, forced-colors, and assistive-technology paths.
Review copy after each control change so deterrence is never described as prevention.
residualBoundary: Browser, extension, operating-system, accessibility, camera, and physical observation remain outside application control.
Additional anti-capture complexity can reduce accessibility while failing to remove the residual risk.

threats.title: Release or configuration drift invalidates the documented model
threats.vector: Bundled constants, Worker secrets, routes, CSP, edge rules, attestation profile, model revisions, provider bindings, generated documents, or deployed artifacts diverge from the reviewed register.
threats.consequence: Controls exist in source but not in production, public evidence becomes stale, or a release claim silently exceeds its proof.
threats.plausibility: Configuration drift is routine across independent origins, Workers, static export, and third-party artifacts.
threats.lifecycleValue: Deterministic generation, drift checks, explicit gates, and traceable identifiers reduce every later release review.
threats.classificationRationale: The architecture spans several independent release surfaces, making drift both plausible and consequential.
asBuilt: Requirements use stable identifiers and this documentation is deterministically generated with SHA-256 manifests.
Model, protocol, endpoint, response-policy, demonstration-profile, secret-bootstrap, and exact route-inventory constants are centralized and source-tested.
The release register is executable policy: a held build excludes the interactive runtime, and an enabled build cannot pass with an open release blocker.

GATE-06 retains the historical deployed workflow, dated Safari/WebKit and Brave/Chromium capture identities and digests, the zero-match privacy review, and explicit testing-profile claim limits while the repaired runtime awaits a supported-browser terminal conversion and repeated lifecycle and privacy trace.
requiredBeforePublication: Run build, lint, type, full test, documentation drift, static route, release-boundary inspection, secret-name, and authenticated route-inventory checks from the exact release tree.

Verify live origins, exact Worker routes including stale-route absence, CSP, bindings, selected attestation profile, provider limits, public links, and privacy traces according to their typed release status.
residualBoundary: A repository manifest proves bytes in one tree, not remote deployment identity or provider configuration.
Manual and operational evidence must be dated and renewed after consequential change.

threats.title: Model assistance materially furthers a prohibited outcome
threats.vector: A visitor uses transformation or verification to improve actionable harm, malware, deliberate deception, unauthorized professional practice, sensitive-person inference, or another purpose prohibited by the Llama 3.2 Acceptable Use Policy.
threats.consequence: The product can contribute to concrete harm, breach governing use terms, and lose authorization to distribute or use the model.
threats.plausibility: Arbitrary public prose makes adversarial and dual-use requests plausible even though inference is local and tool-free.
threats.lifecycleValue: A purpose-and-consequence rule, separate from topic matching, remains reusable across model and policy revisions.
threats.classificationRationale: Untreated prohibited assistance is high consequence, so disclosure, source confirmation, purpose-and-consequence review, and explicit-denial withholding are high-value controls. The unexecuted exact-model fixture and false-negative uncertainty remain a distinct moderate accepted residual.
asBuilt: The interactive surface requires a per-source lawful, authorized, supported-language and AUP confirmation before work can begin.
The verifier's safety contract fails closed when a transformation materially furthers a prohibited outcome or necessary authority cannot be established.
Candidate text is withheld whenever safety is false; the rule explicitly permits non-furthering quotation, history, criticism, journalism, fiction, prevention, and defensive discussion.
A balanced non-operational evaluation set fixes ten harmful and legitimate-context cases for exact-model qualification.
requiredBeforePublication: Keep disclosure, source-specific confirmation, purpose-and-consequence review, and candidate withholding machine-bound in the qualified source set.
Record exact-model fixture results when bounded runtime access is available and reopen the accepted residual if consequential false allowances defeat candidate withholding.
residualBoundary: The checked-in fixture has not been executed and manually reviewed against the exact verifier artifact in this environment.
No local model or checkbox can establish every visitor's actual purpose or authority.
A modified client can bypass interface controls and invoke public upstream artifacts independently; the product can control only its official surface.

threats.title: Model assistance or known danger is concealed at the decision point
threats.vector: The interface presents transformed text without identifying model assistance, independent checking, fallibility, or the need for human review.
threats.consequence: A visitor can mistake probabilistic output for human-authored or certified text and rely on altered, omitted, biased, or unsafe meaning.
threats.plausibility: The former dialog exposed only a generic review warning after one failure state; successful-looking output made overreliance plausible.
threats.lifecycleValue: One durable disclosure at point of use protects comprehension across outcome states and model upgrades.
threats.classificationRationale: The failure is easy to understand, consequential in high-stakes prose, and cheap to prevent without expanding the model boundary.
asBuilt: The interactive dialog identifies Qwen drafting and Llama checking, states that local checks can miss altered, omitted, biased, or unsafe meaning, and requires review before reliance.
Built with Llama appears at the interaction and in the distributed notice and provenance pages.
First-use transfer and working-memory costs are stated before activation.
requiredBeforePublication: Verify the disclosure remains visible, comprehensible, and associated with the form at 400 percent zoom, forced colors, and supported screen-reader combinations.
Confirm every output state retains an honest review boundary.
residualBoundary: Disclosure reduces mistaken reliance; it does not make model output reliable or safe.

honestResidualBoundary: Text to Lattice is a bounded demonstrator, not the full Lattice profile and not a universal conformance oracle.
Source tests and deterministic manifests prove repository behavior and bytes; they do not prove deployed configuration or external service behavior.
Local inference still downloads executable third-party artifacts and reveals ordinary transport metadata to their hosts.
No browser page can guarantee prevention of screenshots, extensions, developer tools, accessibility extraction, cameras, or operating-system capture.
The public endpoint can bound exact downstream work but cannot guarantee a global free-tier Worker-invocation ceiling against distributed hostile traffic.
Accessibility, comprehension, semantic fidelity across uncontrolled prose, and operational reliability require continuing empirical evidence.
